title: Silas and the Oath
premise: Quentin Blackwood has spent her life as a debt-bound scribe in the valley of Silas's Rest, where the god Silas's wards suppress all magic. When the wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, she learns her temple's ledgers were never records of debt but bindings keeping the valley anchored to reality—and the country beyond it was erased decades ago. Guided by Vess, a smuggler who remembers the world that no longer exists, Quentin must rewrite the binding with herself as its living anchor before the valley dissolves entirely. In the end she chooses to unbind rather than restore, freeing the valley's people into an uncertain new world and finding, for the first time, that she belongs to it by choice rather than by contract.
about_author: Isandro Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing abandoned parish records in remote mountain valleys. Their fiction blends bureaucratic fantasy with quiet, stubborn hope.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A night of routine copying in Silas's Rest is shattered when the border wards fail and every star goes dark at once. Reading the oldest ledger, Quentin realizes the 'debts' are bindings—and her own name appears on the final page. The beat is dread blooming into reluctant purpose: invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: What Vess Carried Across
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with Vess's interludes. She flees the collapsing temple with the master ledger and falls in with Vess, a smuggler whose maps show roads to a country that officially never existed. They bargain, bicker, and begin to trust. The beat is wary connection—two people discovering they were both kept small by the same lie.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the erased border, they find the door out—but it demands a living anchor willing to hold the valley's weight alone. Temple enforcers arrive to force a binding that would enslave Quentin permanently. In the climax she fights not to escape but to refuse the terms, rewriting the oath mid-ritual with Vess and the villagers as co-signatories.

chapters.title: A Country With No Name Yet
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, closing with a shared epilogue voice. The valley survives unbound—magic returns gently, stars reappear one by one, and the old debts burn to ash. Quentin, no longer a scribe of obligations, begins writing a new kind of record: names freely given. The beat is quiet belonging; found family as the first law of a country still being invented.
